source: SLSA Framework (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts)

rules.name: Source - Version Controlled
rules.description: Every change to the source is tracked in a version control system, providing a baseline history of who changed what and when.

rules.name: Source - Verified History
rules.description: The version control system requires strong authentication for all contributors, making it harder for an attacker to inject changes under a false identity.

rules.name: Source - Retained and Reviewed
rules.description: All changes are retained indefinitely and require at least one other trusted person's review before becoming the basis for a build, catching malicious code before it is built.

rules.name: Build - Provenance Exists
rules.description: The build process generates provenance describing how the artifact was produced, even if that provenance is not yet verified or tamper-resistant.

rules.name: Build - Hosted, Signed Provenance
rules.description: The build runs on a hosted build platform that generates authenticated (signed) provenance, so consumers can verify the artifact came from the expected build process.

rules.name: Build - Hardened, Isolated Builds
rules.description: The build platform is hardened against tampering: builds run in isolated, ephemeral environments so that one build cannot influence another, and provenance is non-falsifiable even by the build service operators.

rules.name: Provenance Generation
rules.description: The build service must generate an authenticated provenance document detailing what was built, how it was built, and its dependencies.

rules.name: Dependencies Completeness
rules.description: The provenance document must list all dependencies used to build the artifact, aiding in vulnerability tracing and dependency confusion prevention.

rules.name: Ephemeral Build Environment
rules.description: The build runs in an ephemeral, isolated environment (e.g., a fresh container or VM) to prevent persistence of malicious backdoors between builds.
